unsupported_claims: The method precomputes and stores a set of short random walks starting from each node.
When an edge is added or removed, only stored walks passing through affected nodes are identified and regenerated from the point of change onward.
Update cost scales with the number of affected walks, and the approach applies to PageRank-style estimates.
rationale: The general idea that small changes need only local updates and avoid full recomputation matches the evidence. However, the specific mechanism (stored walks, regenerating those through affected nodes, PageRank-style estimates) is invented, while the paper says the model is iteratively updated with new walks from the changed region in time sub-linear to the whole graph.
